Lessons.Title: Ways to Solve Problems and Show Solutions
ExplanationParagraphs: Original 2021 Grade 3 Unit6 Lesson15, closing applied-problem-solving lesson, from local teacher lesson.html SHA256 56213b64179c765060c4f844d4dac80de665a08209c96ecd2c0fda61d4a1ce97 and preparation.html SHA256 30f4cb2773c2aebf31f83a836dd87863d1cc2e81f8a2c4b2cc284ee55a9b6442. The locally archived public teacher/student text is the mapped source; independently formatted publisher Student Task Statements PDF, seven external image assets, teacher-only student responses and original Cool-down have NOT been inspected or copied. No source pixel parity, academic approval or Stage D is asserted.

Warm-up Number Talk: Divide by 8 (10 minutes) retains four ORIGINAL expressions, 80÷8=10;72÷8=9;96÷8=12;96÷4=24. Source encourages connections: subtract eight from80 to get72, add groups of eight to reach96, and compare dividing96 by4 versus8. Mental strategies may differ; mathematical scalar answers are fixed.

Activity1 A Day at the Fair (25 minutes): original pupil task says SOLVE FOUR problems, in pairs by default (individual poster is allowed). Source order and choice logic are mandatory: solve ENTRY PROBLEM, choose EXACTLY ONE OF TWO time problems, choose EXACTLY ONE OF TWO measurement/mass problems, then solve the closing CORN PROBLEM. Do not treat all six alternatives as six mandatory problems or omit choice. The four selected solutions are organized on one student-created POSTER with equations, units, diagrams/time lines and explained reasoning. Source public printed photographs are contextual and not redistributed.

Original required first problem: entry costs $9 per PERSON. You go with SIX OTHER PEOPLE, so your group contains SEVEN people, NOT six. 7×9=63 dollars. Explain grouping, including yourself; this is a common off-by-one trap.

Original CHOOSE ONE for the start of the day: (a) giant pumpkin weigh-off from 11:12 a.m. to 12:25 p.m., duration 73 minutes =1 hour 13 minutes, crosses noon; OR (b) carnival ended12:10 p.m. after 48 minutes, so it began 11:22 a.m. Teachers accept a correctly marked clock, number line, decomposition or subtraction algorithm. These are alternate choices, not both mandatory.

Original CHOOSE ONE for next activity: (a) seven sheep drink91 liters of water per day equally; each sheep drinks91÷7=13 liters PER DAY; OR (b) butter cow weighs273 kilograms, stated to be277 kilograms LESS than the actual cow, so original cow weighs273+277=550 kilograms. Subtracting 277 from273 would reverse the relationship. Original butter-cow source illustrated addition confirms273+277=550.

Original mandatory last problem: 54 ears of grilled corn in NINE EQUAL ROWS give54÷9=6 ears per row. The images include a strip/tape diagram with total84 and segment12 in the SECTION SUMMARY, not part of the four mandatory fair problems; preserve section summary independently: grower used84 liters,12 liters per seedling,84÷12=7 seedlings. The original section summary also repeats carnival11:22 a.m. and cow550kg as reviews.

Activity2 A Day at the Fair Gallery Walk (10 minutes) is not an extra number problem. Students visit other posters in two roles, with partners taking turns visiting and standing to answer. They must (1) find ONE problem solved using a DIFFERENT strategy than theirs, describe that strategy and why different; (2) describe AT LEAST THREE distinct features that made classmates' maths clear (for example legible units, labeled diagrams, decomposition, ordered steps). Teacher evaluates specificity and communication, not an arbitrary exact text response.

Source synthesis asks which representations and habits of clear explanation students would reuse. MLR7 Compare and Connect and accessibility-expression supports require students to consider why distinct methods can produce the same correct result; first-party independent model answers must not replace the student's own chosen path or creative poster. Restricted publisher Cool-down Problem Solving Reflection is NOT reconstructed from a gated source. Authored tests only, not executed; no CI, Stage D, merge or production.

KeyConcepts.Title: Fair route with real choices
KeyConcepts.Definition: Four selected problems: mandatory entrance, one of two times, one of two water/mass situations, mandatory corn.
KeyConcepts.Rule: 2 mandatory +1 time choice +1 quantity choice =4 pupil-selected problems.

KeyConcepts.Title: Add the narrator to the other people
KeyConcepts.Definition: Six other people plus the speaker total seven tickets.

KeyConcepts.Title: Elapsed clock time
KeyConcepts.Definition: Duration between two times crossing noon can be found by stepping to12:00 and forward.

KeyConcepts.Title: Start time from departure and duration
KeyConcepts.Definition: Subtract elapsed minutes from ending time.
KeyConcepts.Example: 12:10 back10 minutes to noon, then38 more to11:22.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equal groups and comparison
KeyConcepts.Definition: Share liters equally or add the known difference to lighter butter cow.

KeyConcepts.Title: Explain and compare
KeyConcepts.Definition: A poster communicates calculation AND reasoning; alternative sound strategies can yield identical results.
KeyConcepts.Rule: At least one alternative strategy and three clarity features in gallery walk.
KeyConcepts.Example: Tape diagram and equation show the same arithmetic.

WorkedExamples.Title: Mandatory entry
WorkedExamples.Question: $9 per person, with6 OTHER people: total entry?

WorkedExamples.Title: Choose one time path A
WorkedExamples.Question: Pumpkin11:12 AM until12:25 PM. How long?

WorkedExamples.Title: Choose one time path B
WorkedExamples.Question: Carnival ends12:10 PM, lasting48 minutes. Arrival?
Steps: Check forward: 11:22 AM + 38 minutes = noon; another 10 minutes reaches 12:10 PM.

WorkedExamples.Title: Choose one animal path A
WorkedExamples.Question: 91 liters among7 sheep equally, daily?
WorkedExamples.Method: Divide total daily liters by seven.
Steps: Keep liters PER sheep PER day.

WorkedExamples.Title: Choose one animal path B
WorkedExamples.Question: Butter cow273kg,277kg less than actual cow?

WorkedExamples.Title: Mandatory corn
WorkedExamples.Question: 54 ears in9 equal rows; each row?
Steps: Therefore each of the nine equal rows has six ears; nine is the number of rows, not the number per row.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source section summary additional example
WorkedExamples.Question: Pumpkin grower used84L,12L per seedling. How many seedlings?
Steps: Seven seedlings each using 12 L would use 7 × 12 = 84 L, confirming the division.
WorkedExamples.Check: Section summary, not an extra fair choice.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Answer the pumpkin duration as 13 minutes.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: 11:12 AM to12:25 PM crosses noon by one whole hour.

Demand both branches of both original choice questions.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Source says solve FOUR problems, choosing one for each of two decision points.

SummaryPoints: Exactly FOUR fair problems per student route: mandatory $63 entry; one time path73min or11:22AM; one quantity path13L/sheep/day or550kg cow; mandatory6 ears/row.
Original section summary includes extra review84/12=7 seedlings—not a mandatory fifth fair problem.
Gallery walk: different strategy described plus at least three clarity features; first-party poster teacher-assessed.
